newsitem.title: USA: ITT Industries reports profit for latest quarter.
newsitem.headline: ITT Industries reports profit for latest quarter.

text.p: ITT Industries Inc. Wednesday reported a profit for the third quarter after a loss a year ago due to charges tied to the divestment of non-core assets it inherited from the break-up of ITT Corp.

ITT Industries, one of the companies formed by the split-up of ITT Corp. in December of last year, reported a profit of $43.7 million, or 36 cents per share -- even with Wall Street expectations. That compared with a loss of $54.2 million, or 46 cents a share, a year ago.
Excluding the charges for the asset sales, however, the company's operating earnings for the 1995 third quarter were $31.6 million, or 27 cents a share.
Sales were slightly lower at $2.04 billion vs. $2.05 billion a year ago.

"While our third quarter results show progress, we have stated that our goals are higher," said Chairman Travis Engen. "We are continuing to face challenges in our businesses, but we remain committed to our goals of delivering value to our owners through revenue growth and improved margins."
Operating income at ITT Automotive, one of the world's largest independent suppliers of automotive systems and components, was $73.6 million, up 2.6 percent from the same quarter of last year.

ITT Fluid Technology's operating income was $26 million, down $2.2 million from the previous year due primarily to foreign exchange and to the absence of income from a unit divested earlier in the year.
ITT Defence & Electronics' operating income for the quarter rose 4.6 percent to $24.9 million.
ITT Industries is a leading diversified manufacturing company with 1995 sales of $8.4 billion from its three primary business segments: automotive, defence & electronics, and fluid technology.
The company's stock was off 62.5 cents at $22.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
